assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opened a new observational window: the 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos in a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector, followed by the 2017-18 association of a neutrino with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and with Galactic-plane emission. This is detector-driven discovery of the kind I judge most fairly: an instrument conceived to answer a question that could not be answered otherwise, with careful calibration and background rejection behind it. The physics (cosmic-ray origins, multi-messenger astronomy) will last.
assessment.attribution: Francis Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its AMANDA precursor; Christian Spiering was a founding figure of neutrino telescopy (Baikal, AMANDA, IceCube) and long-time spokesperson/leader in the field. A two-person prize is workable. Other leaders (e.g. John Kelley, Albrecht Karle, Baikal pioneers) and the large collaboration complicate credit, and I cannot verify precise roles from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been independently seen in several channels and is supported by ANTARES-era and now KM3NeT results; the TXS association is a roughly 3 sigma-level, single-source statement and the individual source picture is still developing. Recognition would be timely rather than premature, since the existence of astrophysical neutrinos is firmly established.
uncertainties: Whether the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 source identifications are robust enough to be cited, versus resting on the diffuse flux alone.
Fair treatment of Baikal and AMANDA pioneers and of other IceCube leaders is unresolved.
Exact individual roles are from my general knowledge and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration, a limit long thought fundamental, brought electron microscopy to sub-angstrom resolution in TEM and STEM and now underpins atomic-scale imaging across materials science, condensed matter and chemistry. It is an instrumentation breakthrough with a very clear before and after, built through years of patient engineering, which is exactly what I respect. Impact is broad and demonstrably lasting.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the multipole corrector design theory; Haider built the first working TEM corrector (with Rose, Uhlemann and Urban at Heidelberg/EMBL); Krivanek built the STEM corrector (with Dellby, Nellist and Lupini). The Heidelberg and Nion/Cambridge-Oak Ridge streams split between TEM and STEM, and Knut Urban's role is a possible omission from this credited set. The three credited names are a defensible fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independently demonstrated by multiple groups and commercial instruments for roughly two decades. Fully mature, and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether Knut Urban, Nion and Oak Ridge colleagues (not in the credited names) have a claim that complicates a three-person split.
Whether the committee regards this as physics rather than instrumentation for materials and life science.
Facts on individual roles are from memory, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and Ye's implementation brought clock fractional uncertainties to the 10^-18 level, about two orders of magnitude beyond the caesium standard. The consequences include tests of relativity and constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. It is a clear, decisive precision-measurement achievement whose techniques are widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength scheme (2001-03) and demonstrated strontium lattice clocks; Jun Ye's group, with JILA colleagues, pushed accuracy and stability to record levels. The pairing is natural. Others (e.g. Pierre Lemonde, Andrew Ludlow and Hall and Hansch via the frequency comb, which was already recognised in 2005) are adjacent, so there is some credit overlap, but a two-person prize is clean.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) reproduce 10^-18 level performance. Mature. The redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened, but that is not required for recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize for the frequency comb and with Wineland's 2012 ion-clock recognition may make some members regard this as incremental.
Whether Lemonde, Ludlow or Hinkley et al. warrant inclusion is not resolved by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele Z2 theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Molenkamp-group observation in HgTe quantum wells launched topological insulators, a major organizing concept for quantum matter, with a clean theory-to-experiment sequence. This is outside my own expertise, so I weight it using the field's consensus and would want colleague and expert review.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group (with Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes, who predicted the HgTe case) delivered the experimental confirmation. Credit is contested around Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents, and Shoucheng Zhang's death in 2018 removes one natural candidate. The three credited names are reasonable but not uncontroversially complete.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently, with three-dimensional topological insulators and many follow-on materials and platforms. Mature and stable, but the overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize raises a question of the incremental step.
uncertainties: The attribution among Kane-Mele, BHZ, Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents is disputed and I cannot resolve it.
The condensed-matter details lie outside my expertise and I defer to colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022) are a major observational achievement, achieved by tying together a global VLBI array at 1.3 mm with extreme calibration effort. They provide direct imaging evidence for black holes and tests of strong-field gravity. As an instrument builder I value the technique highly.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT and the mm-VLBI development; Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept and co-led the science; Moran was the long-time pioneer of mm-VLBI and Haystack/SMA developments. The result is a collaboration of hundreds, so any three-person selection leaves out essential contributors (e.g. analysis, correlation and imaging leads), and the Nobel rules for large collaborations are a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The images are reproduced by repeated epochs and by independent imaging pipelines, and Sgr A* was added in 2022. Still young: interpretation of spin and jet physics is evolving, so timing could be argued either way.
uncertainties: Collaboration scale makes a fair three-person attribution doubtful.
Model dependence of the inferred black-hole parameters is not fully settled.
Whether the committee views the result as confirmation rather than new physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable system, spawning a large field and a new control knob (twist angle). The prediction-then-experiment story is compelling, though I judge it as an outsider to condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered the correlated and superconducting states (2018). That is a natural theory-experiment trio. Cory Dean, Pablo's collaborators and Allan MacDonald's wider circle also feature, and Cao et al. were the first-author drivers, so some uncertainty remains.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely, but the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism and the role of strain and disorder are still unsettled, and the field is moving quickly. This may be premature relative to the stability I like to see.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Sample-to-sample variation and disorder dependence remain a concern.
Outside my own expertise and I would defer to condensed-matter colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping, cooling and precisely measuring antiprotons, positrons and antihydrogen test CPT symmetry and matter-antimatter asymmetry at very high precision. It is close to my own interest in antimatter, and combines difficult apparatus building with a fundamental question. Results include antihydrogen trapping and 1S-2S spectroscopy at ppt-level and the antiproton magnetic moment.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse led the TRAP/ATRAP efforts and led antiproton/positron measurements; Hangst led ALPHA, which trapped and spectroscopically measured antihydrogen. Others (Rolf Landua, Masaki Hori and Yasunori Yamazaki, Wolfgang Oelert, Eric Hessels) are significant, and ALPHA is a large collaboration, so credit is not entirely clean.
assessment.maturity: Precision results are confirmed by several collaborations (ATRAP, ALPHA, ASACUSA, BASE, AEgIS), but no violation has been seen and the field is still improving, so impact beyond the technique is yet to be demonstrated.
uncertainties: Null results so far on CPT and gravity; the discovery content is the method rather than a new effect.
Credit among ATRAP, ALPHA, ASACUSA and BASE leaders is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned an obscure material class into a leading photovoltaic and optoelectronic semiconductor, with efficiencies rising from a few percent to over 25 percent in about a decade. The physics of defect tolerance and the broad materials impact are significant, though the prize case partly rests on applied engineering.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised solar cell (2009); Park and Gratzel's group made the solid-state cell (2012) and Snaith's group showed the mesosuperstructured and planar architectures. Michael Gratzel, Mercouri Kanatzidis, and others have strong claims, and the set here excludes Gratzel, so the fair configuration is open.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across thousands of groups, but stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability are still being worked out, so long-term durability and lasting impact are not yet proved.
uncertainties: Device stability and large-scale deployment remain unproven.
Allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel and Kanatzidis is unresolved.
Outside my own expertise.
